newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, July 17.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, July 17.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - Britain's FTSE 100 index was dragged modestly lower as profit-taking hit the drugs sector, but the market ended well off the day's lows after faltering on the brink of the 5,000 hurdle. The blue-chip index finished 15.2 points lower at 4,949.0.

FRANKFURT - Shares ended lower, having fallen sharply in high-volume late afternoon trade on profit-taking, weakness on Wall Street and a softer dollar against the mark. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,227.31, up 26.07 points, or 0.62 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,203.91, down 19.78 points, or 0.47 percent.

PARIS - Shares closed sharply lower on profit-taking triggered by an all-time record above the 3,000 level which caused a barrage of sell stop orders from the futures market, dealers said. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,958.59, down 29.42 points, or 0.98 percent.
ZURICH - Shares ended lower as the market grew nervous ahead of Friday's expiry of July contracts on Soffex. The Swiss market index closed at 5,868.3, down 59.2 points, or 1.00 percent.

MILAN - Shares closed at a new record high, fuelled by a new rush of orders from at home and abroad, with selected banking and telecom stocks registering hefty gains. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 14,825, up 444 points, or 3.09 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Shares closed 1.23 percent lower, with a four-day sequence of record high closings coming to an emphatic halt as institutions took profits ahead of Friday's options expiries. The AEX index closed at 953.37, down 11.88 points, or 1.23 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks strode upward by the close, boosted by record winning runs in the Dow industrials and the Nasdaq composite index. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,519.25, up 160.51 points, or 0.79 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks soared to a record close on the continued strength of HSBC Holdings, although profit-taking in the afternoon trimmed the market's intra-day gains, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,706.29, up 260.27 points, or 1.69 percent.

SYDNEY - The share market closed off its highs for the day but had still locked away solid gains by the close as local traders took a bullish lead from record-breaking runs in offshore markets. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,669.70, up 23.30 points, or 0.88 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's all-share index was propped up by gains in the bank-laden financial index which soared to another record closing high as investors snapped up stock on hopes of a cut in interest rates. The All-share index closed at 7,437.1, up 14.3 points, or 0.19 percent. The All Gold index closed at 964.3, down 5.2 points, or 0.05 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,941.2, up 4.8 points, or 0.54 percent.
